Danone sets multiple 2025 ESG commitments, including achieving deforestation‑ and conversion‑free supply chains for key commodities, sourcing 30 % of key ingredients from farms transitioning to regenerative agriculture, and delivering a 36 % reduction in Scope 1 & 2 emissions by 2025.  

Danone’s 2025 targets span nature and climate. The company pledges that by 2025 its supply chains for high‑risk commodities (palm oil, paper, soy, cocoa, animal feed) will be free of deforestation and land‑conversion [Danone’s 2023 Report, p. 242]. It also commits that 30 % of key ingredients will be sourced from farms that have begun regenerative‑agriculture practices by 2025 [Danone’s 2023 Integrated Report, p. 14] and that a new KPI will cut Scope 1 & 2 greenhouse‑gas emissions by 36 % relative to the 2022 baseline by 2025 [Danone’s 2024 Integrated Report, p. 15]. Earlier reporting notes a “no deforestation” target for primary deforestation‑linked commodities with a FY2025 deadline [Danone’s 2022 Report, p. 153].  

- “30% key ingredients we source directly will come from … farms … by 2025” [Danone’s 2023 Integrated Report, p. 14]  
- “Zero deforestation & conversion on key commodities … by 2025” [Danone’s 2023 Report, p. 242]  
- “New KPI: 36% reduction on Scope 1 & 2 by 2025” [Danone’s 2024 Integrated Report, p. 15]  
- “no deforestation … with a target date of FY2025” [Danone’s 2022 Report, p. 153]  

**Limitations**  
The documents provide several 2025 commitments but do not disclose the exact baseline values, scopes, or methodologies for the 36 % Scope 1 & 2 reduction KPI. Details on how the 30 % regenerative‑agriculture sourcing will be measured (e.g., verification standards) are not specified. No quantitative target is given for the deforestation‑free commitment beyond the qualitative statement.
